It does not add\n`POST /route/task`, a second score function, or a second routing decision store.\nThe existing `selected.vendor/model/endpoint_kind` meaning remains observable and\nunchanged; assignment and provenance are additive fields.\n\n## D2 — Preserve compatibility with an optional strict profile\n\nLegacy `task_signals` remains accepted with its current permissive extra-field\nbehavior because existing phase callers send fields such as `write_allow`. A new\noptional `routing_profile` is strict (`extra=forbid`) and types:\n\n- expected duration seconds;\n- scope category (`read-only|bounded-write|broad-write`);\n- interactivity (`interactive|headless`);\n- secret need category (`none|brokered|direct`), never a secret value;\n- positive parallelism;\n- repository shape (`single-package|monorepo|unknown`);\n- roadmap-policy constraints (allowed/excluded lane/vendor sets and an allowed-location set);\n- optional required location, isolation, and dispatch mode.\n\nPydantic validates the external boundary and FastAPI/MCP share the same request model.\nNew response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always\npopulated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\n\n## D3 — Rules are ordered, typed, and versioned\n\n`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml` carries `schema_version`, `policy_version`,\ndispatch-mode defaults, ordered first-match constraint rules, and a local-fallback\ndimension table. A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values,\nranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file\nbytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `constrain` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. Explicit request constraints take precedence;\notherwise the first matching rule that mentions a dimension constrains that dimension.\nThe phase-specific or global dispatch default is used only when no explicit or rule-based\ndispatch mode exists; unmatched location/isolation remain unconstrained. Rules narrow\nfeasibility and never add a second utility score. Changing a rule therefore changes the\nfeasible assignment set without code edits.\n\nThe Docker image copies the file beside `agents.yaml` and the loader resolves it from\n`ROUTING_CONFIG` or the package root, never the process working directory.\n\n## D4 — DG-01 is the only lane source and joins are exact\n\n`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all\nlanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained. For\neach lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when\nthe catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key:\n\n`(catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url)`.\n\n`base_url` and additive lane identity travel through `CandidateInput` and\n`ScoredCandidate`. Agent-name suffixes, provider/publisher guesses, substring matches,\nand fuzzy model names are forbidden. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit\nregistry misses and never become routable candidates.\n\nA watchdog `ConfiguredCatalogSync` job materializes configured non-OpenRouter lane\nmodels in `model_catalog`. `agents.yaml` explicitly sets `catalog_vendor` and\n`endpoint_kind` for those lanes: local subscription CLIs use their exact vendor type plus\n`vendor-cli`; remote SDK lanes use their exact vendor type plus `vendor-sdk`. CLI model\nIDs come from the canonical provider model map; SDK model IDs come only from the lane's\nSDK model/fallback list. The job inserts only missing identity rows, with enabled catalog\navailability and unknown price/posterior, and never overwrites existing pricing,\nposterior, availability, or refresh data. Registry probe/rate-limit state remains the live\nlane-availability source.\n\nOpenRouter/local catalog rows remain owned by their existing refresh/probe jobs; for a\nmulti-publisher OpenRouter lane, exact model/endpoint/base-URL matching must yield one row\nbefore the row's catalog vendor becomes part of the four-field key. Missing or ambiguous\nidentity metadata is an explicit configuration miss, never filled from an agent-name\nsuffix or publisher guess. A real-agents.yaml test proves at least one configured CLI\nlane projects exactly after this bootstrap.\n\nThe routing path constructs a read-only `VendorRegistryService(audit=None)` because the\nrouter persists its own typed exclusions and atomic audit link; this avoids emitting one\ngeneric projection-miss audit row per request. The registry and catalog snapshots are\neach loaded once per request. A registry read or shape failure fails closed as\n`routing-registry-unavailable`; it never falls back to catalog-only scoring. Catalog rows\nwith no exact configured lane projection are retained in `excluded` as\n`catalog:no-configured-lane`, rather than disappearing silently.\n\n## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility\n\nFor each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:\n\n1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;\n2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;\n3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;\n4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;\n5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.\n\nReasons are machine-readable and sanitized. The schema allows null which is correct for backward compatibility.\n\n11. **Potential issue**: The routing-decision.schema.json has \"source\": {\"const\": \"coordinator\"} and \"success\": {\"const\": true}. This means it only represents successful coordinator decisions. What about failed decisions? The design says the RPC is atomic and fails with 503, so there's no failed decision to audit. This seems correct.\n\n12. **Potential issue**: The work-packages.yaml wp-policy-service has \"min_trust_level: 2\" and \"verification_tier_required: B\" for the feature overall, but wp-integration requires \"verification_tier_required: A\". This seems reasonable.\n\n13. **Potential issue**: The routing.yaml fallback section has location_order and isolation_order but no dispatch_mode_order. The design says \"The fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact configured values while the coordinator is unreachable.\" The schema doesn't include dispatch_mode in fallback. This might be intentional (dispatch mode comes from phase defaults), but worth noting.\n\n14. **Potential issue**: The spec.md says \"A periodic configuration-backed job SHALL materialize missing non-OpenRouter catalog identities from explicit lane metadata and the canonical provider model map without overwriting live catalog observations.\" The design D4 describes this as \"ConfiguredCatalogSync job\". This is in wp-policy-service scope (watchdog.py).\n\n15. **Potential issue**: The OpenAPI v1.1 SelectModelRequest has routing_profile as optional with default null. The spec says it's \"optional\" but the design says \"New response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always populated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\" This is consistent.\n\n16. **Potential issue**: The routing.schema.json rule \"when\" object doesn't have \"required\" fields - it only requires minProperties: 1. This means a rule could match on just phase, for example. The design says \"Each rule has a typed when predicate over the profile and a typed constrain block\". This seems intentional for flexibility.\n\n17. **Potential issue**: The work-packages.yaml wp-contract-config has \"role: contracts-author\" while others have \"role: backend-implementer\" with \"archetype: implementer\". This seems correct for the different package types.\n\n18. **Potential issue**: The design D7 says \"The routing_decisions.policy_version column keeps dg-00 scorer version linear-utility-v1; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance.\" This means the database column policy_version is NOT updated to include routing policy version - it stays as the scorer version. The routing policy version/checksum is in the provenance JSONB. This is a design decision that should be explicitly called out.\n\n19. **Potential issue**: The design D8 says \"The existing resolve_archetype_for_phase fallback is not rewritten: disabled, failure, malformed-response, and timeout paths still return the exact dg-00 static ResolvedArchetype object with no added reasons or fields.\" This is good for backward compatibility.\n\n20. **Potential issue**: The tasks.md task 2.6 says \"Materialize explicit configured lane/catalog identities without overwriting live catalog data; prove the real roster yields at least one exact routable projection.\" This is a test requirement.\n\nLet me now formulate the findings. I need to output JSON with findings array, each finding having id, type, criticality, description, disposition, axis, severity.\n\nI should focus on actual issues in the plan, not things that are correctly done. The instructions say \"Report no finding when the plan already resolves the concern.\"\n\nLet me identify actual concerns:\n\n1. **routing.yaml fallback missing dispatch_mode**: The fallback schema only has location_order and isolation_order, but the design mentions \"fallback dimension table\" and the local fallback should return dispatch_mode. This could be a gap.\n\n2. **VendorLane.catalog_vendor nullable in dg-01 but required for exact association in dg-04**: The dg-01 contract has catalog_vendor as nullable in VendorLane. The dg-04 design requires exact match on (catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url). If catalog_vendor is null, the association can't be exact. The design says \"for a multi-publisher OpenRouter lane, exact model/endpoint/base-URL matching must yield one row before the row's catalog vendor becomes part of the four-field key\" - this suggests catalog_vendor might be inferred from the catalog row, not from the lane. But for non-OpenRouter lanes, the lane should have catalog_vendor set. This needs clarification.\n\n3. **Migration 042 RPC atomicity**: The design says migration adds \"one transaction-scoped RPC that inserts the routing_decisions row and a sanitized link-only routing_decision audit-log event atomically.\" This is a database function. This seems fine but should be verified.\n\n4. **Work package wp-policy-service locks vendor_registry.py and watchdog.py**: These are dg-01 files. But the design says \"RoutingService injects/loads VendorRegistryService in process\" - this suggests using the existing service, not modifying it. The watchdog.py changes are for the ConfiguredCatalogSync job which is a dg-04 concern. This might be acceptable.\n\n5. **The routing-decision.schema.json only allows source=\"coordinator\" and success=true**: This means failed routing decisions or local fallback decisions are not represented in this audit event schema. The design says the RPC only fires on success (atomic commit), and local fallback doesn't create an audit event. This seems correct per design.\n\n6. **OpenAPI v1.1 ExcludedAssignment reason pattern**: The pattern is `'^(unavailable|quota:exhausted|(lane|policy|catalog|roadmap|registry|cedar):[a-z0-9-]+)$'`. This includes \"cedar\" which seems like a dg-00 reason prefix. The design D5 says \"DG-00's existing unavailable and quota:exhausted values remain accepted alongside DG-04's namespaced reasons.\" The pattern allows lane:, policy:, catalog:, roadmap:, registry:, cedar:. This seems consistent.\n\n7. **The routing.yaml schema doesn't validate that phase_dispatch_modes references valid phases**: The schema just says additionalProperties with dispatchMode ref. No validation that the phase names are valid. The design D3 says \"A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values, ranges, and phase dispatch defaults\" - so validation happens in the loader, not in JSON schema. This is fine.\n\n8. **The work-packages.yaml wp-integration has empty locks.files but locks feature:task-routing:integration key**: This is fine for an integration package.\n\n9. **Potential missing test**: The tasks.md doesn't explicitly test that the routing.yaml schema_version and policy_version are recorded in provenance. A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values,\nranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file\nbytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `constrain` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. Rules narrow\nfeasibility and never add a second utility score. The design says \"OpenRouter/local catalog rows remain owned by their existing refresh/probe jobs; for a multi-publisher OpenRouter lane, exact model/endpoint/base-URL matching must yield one row before the row's catalog vendor becomes part of the four-field key.\" So for OpenRouter lanes, the catalog_vendor comes from the catalog row, not from the lane config. For non-OpenRouter lanes, the lane should have catalog_vendor set explicitly in agents.yaml.\n\nThe design also says: \"agents.yaml explicitly sets catalog_vendor and endpoint_kind for those lanes: local subscription CLIs use their exact vendor type plus vendor-cli; remote SDK lanes use their exact vendor type plus vendor-sdk.\" So this is addressed.\n\nNow let me look for potential issues:\n\n1. **routing.yaml fallback missing dispatch_mode** - The schema only has location_order and isolation_order in fallback. The design says fallback uses \"the lane's exact configured values\" but dispatch_mode is not in the fallback ordering. This could be a gap since dispatch_mode is a routing dimension.\n\n2. **The openapi v1.1 Candidate.assignment requires `catalog_vendor` but the dg-01 VendorLane has `catalog_vendor` as nullable** - The assignment schema requires catalog_vendor (it's in required array). But if a lane doesn't have catalog_vendor set (like OpenRouter lanes), how is this handled? The design says for OpenRouter, the catalog_vendor comes from the catalog row match. This seems fine.\n\n3. **The routing-decision.schema.json has `source` with const \"coordinator\" and `success` with const true** - This means the audit event only represents successful coordinator decisions. This seems correct per design.\n\n4. **Work-packages.yaml wp-policy-service locks `agent-coordinator/src/vendor_registry.py` and `agent-coordinator/src/watchdog.py`** - These are dg-01 files. This is a cross-cutting concern but may be acceptable.\n\n5. **The design D4 says \"The routing path constructs a read-only VendorRegistryService(audit=None)\"** - This creates a new instance without audit. It does not add\n`POST /route/task`, a second score function, or a second routing decision store.\nThe existing `selected.vendor/model/endpoint_kind` meaning remains observable and\nunchanged; assignment and provenance are additive fields.\n\n## D2 — Preserve compatibility with an optional strict profile\n\nLegacy `task_signals` remains accepted with its current permissive extra-field\nbehavior because existing phase callers send fields such as `write_allow`. A new\noptional `routing_profile` is strict (`extra=forbid`) and types:\n\n- expected duration seconds;\n- scope category (`read-only|bounded-write|broad-write`);\n- interactivity (`interactive|headless`);\n- secret need category (`none|brokered|direct`), never a secret value;\n- positive parallelism;\n- repository shape (`single-package|monorepo|unknown`);\n- roadmap-policy constraints (allowed/excluded lane/vendor sets and an allowed-location set);\n- optional required location, isolation, and dispatch mode.\n\nPydantic validates the external boundary and FastAPI/MCP share the same request model.\nNew response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always\npopulated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\n\n## D3 — Rules are ordered, typed, and versioned\n\n`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml` carries `schema_version`, `policy_version`,\ndispatch-mode defaults, ordered first-match constraint rules, and a local-fallback\ndimension table. A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values,\nranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file\nbytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `constrain` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. Explicit request constraints take precedence;\notherwise the first matching rule that mentions a dimension constrains that dimension.\nThe phase-specific or global dispatch default is used only when no explicit or rule-based\ndispatch mode exists; unmatched location/isolation remain unconstrained. Rules narrow\nfeasibility and never add a second utility score. Changing a rule therefore changes the\nfeasible assignment set without code edits.\n\nThe Docker image copies the file beside `agents.yaml` and the loader resolves it from\n`ROUTING_CONFIG` or the package root, never the process working directory.\n\n## D4 — DG-01 is the only lane source and joins are exact\n\n`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all\nlanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained. For\neach lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when\nthe catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key:\n\n`(catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url)`.\n\n`base_url` and additive lane identity travel through `CandidateInput` and\n`ScoredCandidate`. Agent-name suffixes, provider/publisher guesses, substring matches,\nand fuzzy model names are forbidden. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit\nregistry misses and never become routable candidates.\n\nThe registry and catalog snapshots are each loaded once per request. A registry read or\nshape failure fails closed as `routing-registry-unavailable`; it never falls back to\ncatalog-only scoring. Catalog rows with no exact configured lane projection are retained\nin `excluded` as `catalog:no-configured-lane`, rather than disappearing silently.\n\n## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility\n\nFor each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:\n\n1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;\n2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;\n3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;\n4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;\n5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.\n\nReasons are machine-readable and sanitized. Only feasible lane/model candidates enter\nthe existing `score_and_rank`; DG-04 does not duplicate quality, posterior, cost,\nlatency, headroom, or exploration math. Multiple lanes may project the same catalog\nmodel, so the final stable order is `(-score, agent_id, catalog identity)`.\nLocation and isolation constraints use exact equality and dispatch mode uses exact\nmembership in the lane's configured modes; DG-04 does not infer an isolation-strength\nordering.\n\n## D6 — Assignment and provenance are additive\n\nA successful response adds top-level:\n\n- `assignment`: exact `agent_id`, `vendor_type`, `policy_vendor`,\n  `catalog_vendor`, location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base\n  URL;\n- `provenance`: source (`coordinator` or `local-static`), policy version/checksum,\n  matched rule IDs, rationale, persistence flag, durable-audit flag, and exact\n  lane/catalog key.\n\nThe selected candidate and every alternative carry their own additive `assignment`, while\nthe response retains the selected candidate's assignment/provenance at top level for\nconvenience. Existing selected-candidate fields remain intact for older consumers.\nExcluded assignments use a typed shape containing lane/catalog identity and a bounded\nmachine-readable reason.\n\n## D7 — Durable routing record is authoritative; audit event is linked\n\nThe existing `routing_decisions` row is the authoritative durable routing audit. Its\nsanitized `request` stores only declared task signals and the strict routing profile;\npermissive legacy extras such as `write_allow` are never persisted. Its `selected` object\nstores selected assignment plus provenance, and every item in `alternatives` stores its\nown assignment. `excluded` stores typed exclusion records. These are additive JSONB\nshapes and require no new table columns.\n\nMigration `042_atomic_routing_audit.sql` adds one transaction-scoped RPC that inserts the\n`routing_decisions` row and a sanitized link-only `routing_decision` audit-log event\natomically. The event contains only decision ID, selected agent/model, routing-policy\nversion/checksum, source, and success. The service awaits the RPC result and returns only\nafter both rows commit. RPC failure rolls back both writes and produces HTTP 503 detail\n`routing-durability-unavailable`; the MCP mirror returns its existing 503 error envelope.\nFire-and-forget `AuditService.log_operation()` is not used for this invariant, and neither\nan orphan decision nor an orphan audit link is observable. Existing dg-00 callers still\ntake their exact static fallback on any non-200 response.\n\nThe `routing_decisions.policy_version` column keeps dg-00 scorer version\n`linear-utility-v1`; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance. No raw\nsecret, environment value, prompt, free-form task-signal extra, or unbounded path list\nenters either record; only typed/bounded categories and rationale enter persistence.\n\n## D8 — Local fallback is configuration-derived and honest\n\nA skills-side bridge/helper may fall back only after transport timeout/unreachability. It\nloads the checkout's validated `routing.yaml`, `agents.yaml`, and archetype model map,\nthen combines the caller's already-resolved static provider/model with the fallback\ndimension order. It never embeds a roster, fabricates availability, or performs fuzzy\nassociation.\n\nThe response has the normal assignment shape plus `fallback=true`,\n`source=local-static`, `persisted=false`, `durable_audit=false`, and a bounded\nfailure reason. Its catalog key is null because no live catalog join occurred. A local\nUUID is explicitly not retrievable from coordinator decision storage. Missing or invalid\nconfiguration fails loud; the helper does not invent permissive defaults.\n\nThe fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact\nconfigured values while the coordinator is unreachable. It is not an isolation-strength\nprecedence or enforcement policy. The reusable helper lives in\n`skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/routing_fallback.py`, resolves repository config from\nan explicit root or discovered checkout root, and is used by bridge and HTTP-proxy\ndegradation paths.\n\nThe existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` fallback is not rewritten: disabled,\nfailure, malformed-response, and timeout paths still return the exact dg-00 static\n`ResolvedArchetype` object with no added reasons or fields.\n\n## D9 — DG-05/DG-06 boundaries remain closed\n\nDG-04 carries the lane's current configured isolation as data and may filter an explicit\nrequest. It does not define per-mode overrides, the isolation precedence ladder, or\nenforcement; DG-05 owns that contract. It does not call routing before `dispatch_fn`,\nchange `phase_agent.py`, redispatch work, or add loop caps; DG-06 owns obedience.\nNo sandbox is launched; DG-07 owns enforcement.\n\n## D10 — Test-first packages and validation\n\nContract/config tests fail first, followed by pure policy/association tests, then service\nand transport/fallback tests.      1	# Design: Make the orchestrator obey the router
     2	
     3	## Decision D1 — Routing is injected at the host seam
     4	
     5	The roadmap state machine accepts a routing resolver protocol and invokes it before
     6	every synchronous `execute_roadmap` host dispatch. The resolver is responsible for bridge/coordinator access; the
     7	state machine never imports a vendor SDK or executes a model directly. Legacy callers
     8	may omit the resolver during migration, but a configured resolver fails closed when it
     9	is unavailable, raises, or returns malformed data.
    10	
    11	## Decision D2 — Dispatch context is immutable and versioned
    12	
    13	Every routed attempt carries schema version 1, the router's durable `decision_id`, the
    14	roadmap item and phase, an attempt number, a dispatch/ledger work ID, and the complete
    15	selected assignment. Canonical isolation is copied to the host envelope as one of
    16	`none`, `worktree`, or `sandbox`. The state machine validates and deep-copies this
    17	context so host code cannot mutate the router's decision in place.
    18	
    19	## Decision D3 — Completion must prove the active routed attempt
    20	
    21	A routed host result is terminal only when its proof echoes the durable active decision
    22	ID, dispatch work ID, observed agent ID, and expected ledger status. Completed work
    23	advances the phase. Capacity failures first persist the policy decision: WAIT preserves
    24	the lane and pause window, while SWITCH excludes the observed lane and requests a fresh
    25	router decision. Failed work closes the attempt and fails the item. Vendor-limit
    26	status, policy action, and any WAIT pause window are committed in one checkpoint save;
    27	a configured cost ceiling without authoritative routed cost evidence fails closed.
    28	The host-owned
    29	resolver/reconciler boundary supplies coordinator ledger evidence; the state machine
    30	validates that evidence against its checkpoint and never treats host mutation of the
    31	dispatch copy as authority. Retrying the same decision or accepting a stale,
    32	mismatched, unavailable, or unknown result fails closed.
    33	
    34	## Decision D4 — Loop safety is durable state
    35	
    36	The checkpoint records a global iteration count, a durable-progress fingerprint,
    37	consecutive no-progress count, and the most recent escalation. A durable item, phase,
    38	or ledger transition changes the fingerprint and resets the no-progress count. Hitting
    39	either configured cap checkpoints the escalation before execution parks, so restart
    40	cannot erase the guard or duplicate the escalation. Resumption requires an explicit
    41	host acknowledgement; prepared work is reconciled before any new submission, and a
    42	counter-based escalation parks again unless the host intentionally raises the relevant
    43	positive cap.
    44	
    45	## Decision D5 — Additive migration preserves current callers
    46	
    47	The opt-in delegated batch lifecycle is outside this change: it prepares requests and
    48	applies collected results through a distinct durable contract rather than invoking the
    49	synchronous phase `dispatch_fn` seam. Routing that lifecycle requires a separate change.
    50	
    51	The routing resolver and safety state are additive. Existing checkpoints deserialize
    52	with empty safety state, and callers without a resolver retain the current host-assisted
    53	path until the skill host wires the bridge. The new global iteration and no-progress
    54	guards intentionally bound both legacy and routed execution; legacy policies configured
    55	above the no-progress cap may park at the safety boundary first. Once a resolver is supplied, no implicit
    56	static route or unverified success is accepted.
     1	## ADDED Requirements
     2	
     3	### Requirement: Executed Routing Decisions
     4	
     5	`autopilot-roadmap` SHALL obtain and durably persist a validated routing decision before each synchronous `execute_roadmap` host dispatch. The immutable dispatch context SHALL include a decision identifier, selected agent/vendor/model/location, canonical dg-05 isolation, dispatch mode, and ledger work/attempt correlation. The host seam SHALL preserve this context unchanged; the state machine SHALL not call a model SDK or select a vendor locally.
     6	
     7	#### Scenario: Ledger-verified vendor switch
     8	
     9	WHEN a submitted attempt reports a vendor-limit result
    10	AND active roadmap policy authorizes switching lanes
    11	THEN the orchestrator SHALL resolve a fresh alternate assignment excluding the observed limited lane
    12	AND persist a new attempt before redispatching the same item and phase
    13	AND accept success only when the terminal VendorResultEnvelope/ledger completion matches that attempt's decision identifier and observed lane
    14	AND reject a stale, mismatched, or unavailable completion without treating the phase as complete.
    15	
    16	#### Scenario: Routed vendor limit honors wait policy
    17	
    18	WHEN a routed attempt reports a vendor-limit result
    19	AND active roadmap policy requires waiting
    20	THEN the orchestrator SHALL close the attempt as vendor-limited and persist `policy_action: wait`
    21	AND SHALL persist the vendor pause and reset window without resolving or dispatching an alternate lane.
    22	
    23	#### Scenario: Router unavailable
    24	
    25	WHEN no validated routing decision can be obtained from the configured resolver
    26	THEN the orchestrator SHALL use only a declared static fallback assignment with canonical isolation
    27	OR SHALL checkpoint a fail-closed escalation
    28	AND SHALL NOT dispatch with an un-routed context.
    29	
    30	### Requirement: Roadmap Loop Safety Caps
    31	
    32	The roadmap execution loop SHALL enforce durable global iteration and no-progress safeguards. Their counters and last durable-progress fingerprint SHALL be checkpointed before each dispatch and survive a resumed process.
    33	
    34	#### Scenario: Stuck dispatch trips the cap
    35	
    36	WHEN the configured iteration cap is reached or consecutive iterations produce no durable item, phase, or correlated-ledger transition
    37	THEN the loop SHALL checkpoint an explicit parked/escalated outcome and return it without continuing to dispatch.
    38	
    39	#### Scenario: Resume does not duplicate a submitted attempt
    40	
    41	WHEN a process stops after persisting a prepared attempt and before terminal completion
    42	THEN a resumed process SHALL reconcile the correlated ledger state before any new submission
    43	AND SHALL NOT issue a duplicate dispatch for that attempt.

     1	"""Grok (xAI) agent backend for evaluation.
     2	
     3	Executes tasks via the `grok` CLI (xAI subscription, never OpenRouter) and reads
     4	a structured JSON envelope rather than scraping stdout.
     5	
     6	Empirical Phase 1 findings (design.md § Empirical CLI findings):
     7	- E2: the prompt is delivered on stdin via ``--prompt-file /dev/stdin``.
     8	- E6: ``--output-format json`` emits an envelope whose conforming payload lives
     9	  under ``.structuredOutput``; token usage, when present, is under ``.usage``.
    10	"""
    11	
    12	from __future__ import annotations
    13	
    14	import asyncio
    15	import json
    16	import os
    17	import shutil
    18	import time
    19	from typing import Any
    20	
    21	from ..config import AblationFlags, AgentBackendConfig
    22	from ..metrics import TokenUsage
    23	from .base import BackendResult
    24	
    25	
    26	class GrokBackend:
    27	    """Backend that executes tasks via the `grok` CLI with JSON output."""
    28	
    29	    def __init__(
    30	        self,
    31	        command: str = "grok",
    32	        args: list[str] | None = None,
    33	        env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    34	        timeout_seconds: int = 300,
    35	    ) -> None:
    36	        self._command = command
    37	        self._args = args or []
    38	        self._env = env or {}
    39	        self._timeout = timeout_seconds
    40	
    41	    @property
    42	    def name(self) -> str:
    43	        return "grok"
    44	
    45	    def _build_command(self, prompt: str) -> list[str]:
    46	        """Argv requesting a JSON envelope, prompt fed on stdin (E2/E6)."""
    47	        return [
    48	            self._command,
    49	            "--prompt-file",
    50	            "/dev/stdin",
    51	            "--output-format",
    52	            "json",
    53	            *self._args,
    54	        ]
    55	
    56	    def _stdin_input(self, prompt: str) -> str | None:
    57	        """`grok` reads the prompt from stdin (`--prompt-file /dev/stdin`)."""
    58	        return prompt
    59	
    60	    @staticmethod
    61	    def _extract_usage(envelope: dict[str, Any]) -> TokenUsage:
    62	        usage = envelope.get("usage") or {}
    63	        input_tokens = int(usage.get("input_tokens", usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0)))
    64	        output_tokens = int(
    65	            usage.get("output_tokens", usage.get("completion_tokens", 0))
    66	        )
    67	        total = int(usage.get("total_tokens", input_tokens + output_tokens))
    68	        return TokenUsage(
    69	            input_tokens=input_tokens,
    70	            output_tokens=output_tokens,
    71	            total_tokens=total,
    72	        )
    73	
    74	    def _parse_envelope(self, stdout: str) -> tuple[str, TokenUsage]:
    75	        """Parse the ``--output-format json`` envelope (E6).
    76	
    77	        The structured result lives under ``.structuredOutput``; if absent, fall
    78	        back to a plain text field. Raises ``ValueError`` on non-JSON output so
    79	        the caller can surface a parse failure rather than silently succeeding.
    80	        """
    81	        try:
    82	            envelope = json.loads(stdout)
    83	        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
    84	            raise ValueError(
    85	                f"grok did not emit a JSON envelope: {exc}"
    86	            ) from exc
    87	
    88	        if not isinstance(envelope, dict):
    89	            raise ValueError("grok JSON envelope is not an object")
    90	
    91	        if "structuredOutput" in envelope:
    92	            output = json.dumps(envelope["structuredOutput"])
    93	        else:
    94	            output = str(
    95	                envelope.get("output")
    96	                or envelope.get("text")
    97	                or envelope.get("content")
    98	                or ""
    99	            )
   100	        return output, self._extract_usage(envelope)
   101	
   102	    async def execute_task(
   103	        self,
   104	        task_description: str,
   105	        affected_files: list[str],
   106	        working_dir: str,
   107	        ablation: AblationFlags,
   108	        timeout_seconds: int = 300,
   109	    ) -> BackendResult:
   110	        """Execute a task via the `grok` CLI and parse the JSON envelope."""
   111	        timeout = timeout_seconds if timeout_seconds is not None else self._timeout
   112	        start_time = time.time()
   113	
   114	        files_context = "\n".join(f"- {f}" for f in affected_files)
   115	        prompt = f"{task_description}\n\nFiles to work on:\n{files_context}"
   116	
   117	        cmd = self._build_command(prompt)
   118	
   119	        try:
   120	            env = {**os.environ, **self._env}
   121	            process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
   122	                *cmd,
   123	                stdin=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
   124	                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
   125	                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
   126	                cwd=working_dir,
   127	                env=env,
   128	            )
   129	            stdin_bytes = (self._stdin_input(prompt) or "").encode("utf-8")
   130	            stdout, stderr = await asyncio.wait_for(
   131	                process.communicate(input=stdin_bytes), timeout=timeout
   132	            )
   133	            wall_clock = time.time() - start_time
   134	
   135	            raw = stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
   136	            err_output = stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
   137	
   138	            if process.returncode != 0:
   139	                return BackendResult(
   140	                    success=False,
   141	                    output=raw,
   142	                    wall_clock_seconds=wall_clock,
   143	                    error=err_output or f"grok exited {process.returncode}",
   144	                )
   145	
   146	            try:
   147	                output, usage = self._parse_envelope(raw)
   148	            except ValueError as exc:
   149	                return BackendResult(
   150	                    success=False,
   151	                    output=raw,
   152	                    wall_clock_seconds=wall_clock,
   153	                    error=str(exc),
   154	                )
   155	
   156	            return BackendResult(
   157	                success=True,
   158	                output=output,
   159	                wall_clock_seconds=wall_clock,
   160	                token_usage=usage,
   161	            )
   162	        except TimeoutError:
   163	            return BackendResult(
   164	                success=False,
   165	                wall_clock_seconds=time.time() - start_time,
   166	                error=f"Timeout after {timeout}s",
   167	            )
   168	        except FileNotFoundError:
   169	            return BackendResult(
   170	                success=False,
   171	                error=f"Command not found: {self._command}",
   172	            )
   173	
   174	    async def health_check(self) -> bool:
   175	        """Check if the `grok` CLI is available."""
   176	        return shutil.which(self._command) is not None
   177	
   178	    @classmethod
   179	    def from_config(cls, config: AgentBackendConfig) -> GrokBackend:
   180	        return cls(
   181	            command=config.command,
   182	            args=config.args,
   183	            env=config.env,
   184	            timeout_seconds=config.timeout_seconds,
   185	        )
     1	"""Antigravity (agy) agent backend for evaluation.
     2	
     3	Executes tasks via the Antigravity CLI (`agy`) in headless mode. Antigravity is
     4	Google's agentic harness and runs the Gemini model family; the CLI is
     5	Claude-shaped, emitting plain markdown/text to stdout.
     6	
     7	Empirical Phase 1 finding E7 (design.md § Empirical CLI findings): `agy` ignores
     8	stdin and a trailing positional — the prompt must be the VALUE of ``--prompt``
     9	(``-p``). This backend therefore attaches the prompt to the flag, unlike the
    10	stdin/positional shapes used by grok and pi.
    11	"""
    12	
    13	from __future__ import annotations
    14	
    15	import asyncio
    16	import os
    17	import shutil
    18	import time
    19	
    20	from ..config import AblationFlags, AgentBackendConfig
    21	from ..metrics import TokenUsage
    22	from .base import BackendResult
    23	
    24	
    25	class AntigravityBackend:
    26	    """Backend that executes tasks via the Antigravity (`agy`) CLI."""
    27	
    28	    def __init__(
    29	        self,
    30	        command: str = "agy",
    31	        args: list[str] | None = None,
    32	        env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    33	        timeout_seconds: int = 300,
    34	    ) -> None:
    35	        self._command = command
    36	        self._args = args or []
    37	        self._env = env or {}
    38	        self._timeout = timeout_seconds
    39	
    40	    @property
    41	    def name(self) -> str:
    42	        return "antigravity"
    43	
    44	    def _build_command(self, prompt: str) -> list[str]:
    45	        """Argv for a headless run (E7: prompt is the value of ``--prompt``)."""
    46	        return [self._command, "--prompt", prompt, *self._args]
    47	
    48	    def _stdin_input(self, prompt: str) -> str | None:
    49	        """`agy` reads the prompt from the flag, never stdin (E7)."""
    50	        return None
    51	
    52	    async def execute_task(
    53	        self,
    54	        task_description: str,
    55	        affected_files: list[str],
    56	        working_dir: str,
    57	        ablation: AblationFlags,
    58	        timeout_seconds: int = 300,
    59	    ) -> BackendResult:
    60	        """Execute a task via the `agy` CLI."""
    61	        timeout = timeout_seconds if timeout_seconds is not None else self._timeout
    62	        start_time = time.time()
    63	
    64	        files_context = "\n".join(f"- {f}" for f in affected_files)
    65	        prompt = f"{task_description}\n\nFiles to work on:\n{files_context}"
    66	
    67	        cmd = self._build_command(prompt)
    68	
    69	        try:
    70	            env = {**os.environ, **self._env}
    71	            process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
    72	                *cmd,
    73	                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
    74	                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
    75	                cwd=working_dir,
    76	                env=env,
    77	            )
    78	            stdout, stderr = await asyncio.wait_for(
    79	                process.communicate(), timeout=timeout
    80	            )
    81	            wall_clock = time.time() - start_time
    82	
    83	            output = stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    84	            err_output = stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    85	
    86	            return BackendResult(
    87	                success=process.returncode == 0,
    88	                output=output,
    89	                wall_clock_seconds=wall_clock,
    90	                token_usage=TokenUsage(),  # agy CLI does not report tokens
    91	                error=err_output if process.returncode != 0 else None,
    92	            )
    93	        except TimeoutError:
    94	            return BackendResult(
    95	                success=False,
    96	                wall_clock_seconds=time.time() - start_time,
    97	                error=f"Timeout after {timeout}s",
    98	            )
    99	        except FileNotFoundError:
   100	            return BackendResult(
   101	                success=False,
   102	                error=f"Command not found: {self._command}",
   103	            )
   104	
   105	    async def health_check(self) -> bool:
   106	        """Check if the `agy` CLI is available."""
   107	        return shutil.which(self._command) is not None
   108	
   109	    @classmethod
   110	    def from_config(cls, config: AgentBackendConfig) -> AntigravityBackend:
   111	        return cls(
   112	            command=config.command,
   113	            args=config.args,
   114	            env=config.env,
   115	            timeout_seconds=config.timeout_seconds,
   116	        )

   508	def _last_fix_diff(
   509	    worktree_path: Path,
   510	    pre_fix_rev: str | None = None,
   511	) -> str:
   512	    """Diff of commits plus dirty tree since ``pre_fix_rev``.
   513	
   514	    ``git diff HEAD`` is empty when the callback committed its edits, so
   515	    round N+1 would hunt an empty-diff marker. ``git diff <pre_fix_rev>``
   516	    compares the working tree to the snapshot, which includes both the
   517	    new HEAD and leftover dirty files. Dirty-only is the fallback when
   518	    no snapshot is available.
   519	    """
   520	    if pre_fix_rev:
   521	        diff = _git(worktree_path, "diff", pre_fix_rev)
   522	        if diff:
   523	            return diff
   524	    return _git(worktree_path, "diff", "HEAD")

   616	) -> int:
   617	    """Run apply-outcome and escalate on failure (design D9).
   618	
   619	    Invokes ``runner.py apply-outcome`` (via *apply_runner*, injectable for
   620	    tests). On a zero exit, leaves the state as apply-outcome wrote it and
   550	    with the flags its own CLI needs for a plain, non-schema-constrained
   551	    prompt (``--print`` for claude, ``exec -s workspace-write`` for codex,
   552	    ``--prompt-file /dev/stdin`` for grok, and so on) — using a single
   553	    hard-coded Claude flag set (``--print --allowedTools``) here made the
   554	    pass silently no-op for every other vendor, since those flags mean
   555	    nothing to their CLIs. This reads that per-vendor mode instead. Returns
   556	    ``None`` (never raises) when the binary is not on PATH, or when the
   557	    vendor declares no synchronous ``alternative``/``quick`` mode to build
   558	    the command from — callers pass that straight to :func:`run` as
   559	    ``caller=None``, which skips gracefully rather than guessing flags.
   560	
   561	    Read-only-ness is a property of the fact-check prompt (it only ever
   562	    asks for a verdict, never invites an edit), not of the CLI's own
   563	    tool-permission flags — the same design already used for grok/agy/pi's
   564	    review-mode dispatch (see agents.yaml's comments on those vendors).

     1	"""Eval-backend registry and factory.
     2	
     3	The single place that maps a supported roster name to its ``AgentBackend``
     4	adapter. This is the pluggable-adapter seam the roster migration rides on:
     5	adding, retiring, or reflagging a harness is a one-line change here plus an
     6	adapter module, and everything else routes through :func:`build_backend`.
     7	
     8	Requesting a retired harness (the removed Gemini/Jules backend) raises a
     9	structured :class:`UnknownBackendError` naming the supported roster, satisfying
    10	the evaluation-framework requirement "requesting one SHALL raise a structured
    11	error naming the supported roster".
    12	"""
    13	
    14	from __future__ import annotations
    15	
    16	from ..config import AgentBackendConfig
    17	from .antigravity import AntigravityBackend
    18	from .base import AgentBackend
    19	from .claude_code import ClaudeCodeBackend
    20	from .codex import CodexBackend
    21	from .grok import GrokBackend
    22	from .pi import PiBackend
    23	
    24	# Supported roster: name (matches each backend's ``.name``) → adapter class.
    25	SUPPORTED_BACKENDS: dict[str, type[AgentBackend]] = {
    26	    "claude_code": ClaudeCodeBackend,
    27	    "codex": CodexBackend,
    28	    "antigravity": AntigravityBackend,
    29	    "grok": GrokBackend,
    30	    "pi": PiBackend,
    31	}
    32	
    33	
    34	class UnknownBackendError(ValueError):
    35	    """Raised when a backend name is not part of the supported roster.
    36	
    37	    Names the supported roster so a caller migrating off a retired harness
    38	    (such as the removed Gemini/Jules backend) can see what to target instead.
    39	    """
    40	
    41	    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
    42	        self.name = name
    43	        supported = ", ".join(sorted(SUPPORTED_BACKENDS))
    44	        super().__init__(
    45	            f"Unknown agent backend {name!r}. "
    46	            f"Supported roster: {supported}."
    47	        )
    48	
    49	
    50	def get_backend_class(name: str) -> type[AgentBackend]:
    51	    """Return the adapter class for a supported roster *name*.
    52	
    53	    Raises:

  2262	def select_validator_vendor(
  2263	    candidates: list[str],
  2264	    change_id: str,
  2265	    agents_yaml_path: Path | None = None,
  2266	    repo_root: Path | None = None,
  2267	    state_path: Path | None = None,
  2268	) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
  2269	    """Select a validator vendor for *change_id*.
  2270	
  2271	    Implements the worker-vs-validator vendor-diversity policy:
  2272	
  2273	    * If policy is disabled (``enforce_for`` does not include
  2274	      ``worker_vs_validator``), returns the first candidate with a
  2275	      "policy disabled" log message.
  2276	    * Otherwise, excludes vendors recorded as workers for this change.
  2277	    * If the resulting candidate set is empty, returns the first original
  2278	      candidate and logs a warning ("only N vendor available, violating
  2279	      policy but continuing"). Does NOT raise — fallback is warn_and_continue.
  2280	
  2281	    Records the selected validator vendor in dispatch state for downstream
  2282	    invocations.
  2283	
  2284	    Returns a tuple ``(selected_vendor, log_message)``. ``selected_vendor`` is
  2285	    None only when *candidates* is empty.
  2286	    """
  2287	    if not candidates:
  2288	        return None, "vendor_diversity: no candidates available"
  2289	
  2290	    policy = load_vendor_diversity_policy(agents_yaml_path)
  2291	    enforce_for = policy.get("enforce_for") or []
  2292	
  2293	    if "worker_vs_validator" not in enforce_for:
  2294	        selected = candidates[0]
  2295	        msg = "vendor_diversity: policy disabled by config"
  2296	        logger.info(msg)
  2297	        # Still record selection so downstream tooling can audit.
  2298	        state = read_dispatch_state(change_id, repo_root, state_path)
  2299	        validators = list(state.get("validator_vendors", []))
  2300	        if selected not in validators:
  2301	            validators.append(selected)
  2302	        state["validator_vendors"] = validators
  2303	        state.setdefault("worker_vendors", [])
  2304	        state["change_id"] = change_id
  2305	        write_dispatch_state(change_id, state, repo_root, state_path)
  2306	        return selected, msg
  2307	
  2308	    state = read_dispatch_state(change_id, repo_root, state_path)
  2309	    worker_vendors = list(state.get("worker_vendors", []))
  2310	    filtered = [c for c in candidates if c not in worker_vendors]
  2311	
  2312	    if filtered:
  2313	        selected = filtered[0]
  2314	        excluded = ",".join(worker_vendors) if worker_vendors else "(none)"
  2315	        msg = (
  2316	            f"vendor_diversity: excluded {excluded} (worker), "
  2317	            f"selected {selected} (validator) for {change_id}"
  2318	        )
  2319	        logger.info(msg)
  2320	    else:
  2321	        selected = candidates[0]
  2322	        n = len(set(candidates))
  2323	        msg = (
  2324	            f"vendor_diversity: only {n} vendor available "
  2325	            f"({selected}), violating policy but continuing"
  2326	        )
  2327	        logger.warning(msg)
  2328	
  2329	    # Persist the validator selection.
  2330	    validators = list(state.get("validator_vendors", []))
  2331	    if selected not in validators:
  2332	        validators.append(selected)
  2333	    state["validator_vendors"] = validators
  2334	    state.setdefault("worker_vendors", worker_vendors)
  2335	    state["change_id"] = change_id
  2336	    write_dispatch_state(change_id, state, repo_root, state_path)
  2337	
  2338	    return selected, msg

  2345	# Substring markers — same style as classify_error, not a result-path regex.

  2353	def _is_concurrent_git_error(result: ReviewResult) -> bool:
  2354	    """True when a vendor CLI failed because of concurrent git index access."""
  2355	    blob = "\n".join(
  2356	        part for part in (result.error, result.raw_stderr, result.raw_stdout) if part
  2357	    ).lower()
  2358	    return any(marker in blob for marker in _GIT_INDEX_ERROR_MARKERS)

  2361	def _safe_path_component(value: str) -> str:
  2362	    cleaned = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "_", value).strip("._-")
  2363	    return cleaned or "unknown"

  2373	def _main_repo_from_cwd(cwd: Path) -> Path:
  2374	    """Resolve the main repository root even when *cwd* is a linked worktree."""
  2375	    try:
  2376	        proc = subprocess.run(
  2377	            ["git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir"],
  2378	            cwd=str(cwd),
  2379	            capture_output=True,
  2380	            text=True,
  2381	            timeout=15,
  2382	        )
  2383	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
  2384	        return Path(cwd)
  2385	    if proc.returncode != 0 or not proc.stdout.strip():
  2386	        return Path(cwd)
  2387	    git_common = proc.stdout.strip()
  2388	    if git_common == ".git":
  2389	        try:
  2390	            top = subprocess.run(
  2391	                ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
  2392	                cwd=str(cwd),
  2393	                capture_output=True,
  2394	                text=True,
  2395	                timeout=15,
  2396	            )
  2397	        except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
  2398	            return Path(cwd)
  2399	        if top.returncode == 0 and top.stdout.strip():
  2400	            return Path(top.stdout.strip())
  2401	        return Path(cwd)
  2402	    common_path = Path(git_common)
  2403	    if not common_path.is_absolute():
  2404	        common_path = (Path(cwd) / common_path).resolve()
  2405	    if common_path.name == ".git":
  2406	        return common_path.parent
  2407	    return common_path
  2408

  2410	def review_snapshot_path(cwd: Path, round_id: str, vendor: str) -> Path:
  2411	    """``.git-worktrees/.review-snapshots/<round>/<vendor>/`` under the main repo."""
  2412	    root = _main_repo_from_cwd(cwd) / ".git-worktrees" / ".review-snapshots"
  2413	    return root / _safe_path_component(round_id) / _safe_path_component(vendor)

  2416	def create_review_snapshot(cwd: Path, round_id: str, vendor: str) -> Path:
  2417	    """Add a detached throwaway worktree for one vendor retry, then return it."""
  2418	    dest = review_snapshot_path(cwd, round_id, vendor)
  2419	    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  2420	    if dest.exists():
  2421	        destroy_review_snapshot(dest, cwd)
  2422	    subprocess.run(
  2423	        ["git", "worktree", "add", "--detach", str(dest), "HEAD"],
  2424	        cwd=str(cwd),
  2425	        check=True,
  2426	        capture_output=True,
  2427	        text=True,
  2428	        timeout=60,
  2429	    )
  2430	    return dest

  2433	def destroy_review_snapshot(snapshot: Path, git_cwd: Path) -> None:
  2434	    """Remove a review snapshot worktree after collect. Best-effort."""
  2435	    try:
  2436	        subprocess.run(
  2437	            ["git", "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(snapshot)],
  2438	            cwd=str(git_cwd),
  2439	            capture_output=True,
  2440	            text=True,
  2441	            timeout=60,
  2442	            check=False,
  2443	        )
  2444	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
  2445	        logger.warning("Failed to remove review snapshot %s: %s", snapshot, exc)
  2446	    if Path(snapshot).exists():
  2447	        shutil.rmtree(snapshot, ignore_errors=True)
  2448	    try:
  2449	        subprocess.run(
  2450	            ["git", "worktree", "prune"],
  2451	            cwd=str(git_cwd),
  2452	            capture_output=True,
  2453	            text=True,
  2454	            timeout=30,
  2455	            check=False,
  2456	        )
  2457	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
  2458	        pass

  2460	
  2461	def _dispatch_with_snapshot_fallback(
  2462	    *,
  2463	    vendor: str,
  2464	    cwd: Path,
  2465	    round_id: str,
  2466	    run: Callable[[Path], ReviewResult],
  2467	) -> ReviewResult:
  2468	    """Run *run(cwd)*; on concurrent git-index failure, retry on a snapshot."""
  2469	    result = run(cwd)
  2470	    if result.success or not _is_concurrent_git_error(result):
  2471	        return result
  2472	    logger.warning(
  2473	        "Concurrent git access error for %s; retrying on detached snapshot",
  2474	        vendor,
  2475	    )
  2476	    snapshot: Path | None = None
  2477	    try:
  2478	        snapshot = create_review_snapshot(cwd, round_id, vendor)
  2479	        return run(snapshot)
  2480	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — keep the original vendor error

    56	            change_id=str(data["change_id"]),
    57	            phase=str(data["phase"]),
    58	            provider=str(data["provider"]),
    59	            archetype=data.get("archetype"),
    60	            model=data.get("model"),
    61	            prompt=str(data["prompt"]),
    62	            system_prompt=data.get("system_prompt"),
    63	            isolation=data.get("isolation"),
    64	            expected_outcomes=list(data.get("expected_outcomes") or []),
    65	            agent_id=data.get("agent_id"),
    66	        )
    67	
    68	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    69	        return asdict(self)
    70	
    71	
    72	@dataclass
    73	class PhaseDispatchResult:
    74	    schema_version: int = 1
    75	    outcome: str = "failed"
    76	    handoff_id: str = ""
    77	    provider: str = ""
    78	    model_used: str | None = None
    79	    dispatch_tier: str = "fallback"
    80	    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    81	    agent_id: str | None = None
    82	    error_class: str | None = None
    83	    capacity_scope: str | None = None
    84	    capacity_model: str | None = None
    85	    capacity_reset_at: str | None = None

    92	ProviderRunner = Callable[[PhaseDispatchPayload], Any]
    93	
    94	_SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS = {"claude_code", "codex", "antigravity", "grok", "pi", "local"}
    95	_CLAUDE_ALIASES = {"opus", "sonnet", "haiku", "fable"}
    96	
    97	# --- local provider adapter (OpenSpec add-local-model-provider-tier, D2/D5) ---
    98	#
    99	# `local` launches the existing Pi coding-agent harness with its normal file and
   100	# command tools. A one-shot Pi extension registers the distinct `local` provider
   101	# against the operator-run OpenAI-compatible endpoint (llama-server / vLLM /
   102	# Ollama); stdlib urllib remains only for the bounded health probe.
   103	#
   104	# Environment contract:
   105	#   LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL       required to enable; http:// or https:// only;
   106	#                                  includes the API version prefix, e.g.
   107	#                                  "http://gx10.local:8080/v1"
   108	#   LOCAL_INFERENCE_API_KEY        optional bearer token
   109	#   LOCAL_INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY  optional, default 4, clamped to 64; excess
   110	#                                  dispatches queue (per process — see the module
   111	#                                  docstring)
   112	#
   113	# With LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL unset the provider is inert: dispatch returns the
   114	# same structured `fallback` result any unconfigured adapter returns, and no
   115	# network call is made (Rule 4 — safe default).
   116	_LOCAL_PROVIDER = "local"
   117	_LOCAL_DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENCY = 4
   118	# A process cannot usefully hold more in-flight local requests than this, and a
   119	# fat-fingered env value must not turn the gate into an unbounded thread farm.
   120	_LOCAL_MAX_MAX_CONCURRENCY = 64
    60	class ProviderModelMappingError(ValueError):
    61	    """Raised when a provider is paired with a Claude-only model alias."""
    62	
    63	
    64	class LocalTrustBoundaryError(RuntimeError):
    65	    """Raised when a real-mode `local` smoke cannot prove a permitted archetype.
    66	
    67	    The resolver is the single decision point for the `local` trust boundary. If
    68	    it refuses the pairing (or is unreachable, which is indistinguishable from a
    69	    refusal at this layer), the smoke fails here: it must not fall through to a
    70	    hardcoded model and dispatch to the endpoint anyway.
    71	    """
    72	
    73	
    74	def _smoke_phase(provider: str) -> str:
    75	    return _LOCAL_SMOKE_PHASE if provider == _LOCAL_PROVIDER else _DEFAULT_SMOKE_PHASE
    76	
    77	
    78	def _build_payload(
    79	    provider: str,
    80	    model_override: str | None,
    81	    *,
    82	    dry_run: bool = False,
    83	) -> PhaseDispatchPayload:
    84	    if provider != "claude_code" and model_override in _CLAUDE_ALIASES:
    85	        raise ProviderModelMappingError(provider, model_override or "")
    86	
    87	    phase = _smoke_phase(provider)
    88	    state = {
    89	        "loc_estimate": 25,
    90	        "write_allow": ["skills/autopilot/**"],
    91	        "dependencies": [],
    92	    }
    93	    options = phase_agent._build_options(  # noqa: SLF001 - canonical public bridge path
    94	        phase, state, provider=provider
    95	    )
    96	    archetype = state.get("_resolved_archetype")
    97	
    98	    if provider == _LOCAL_PROVIDER:
    99	        if dry_run:
   100	            # Offline fixture; nothing leaves the process.
   101	            archetype = archetype or _LOCAL_DRY_RUN_ARCHETYPE
   102	        elif not archetype:
   103	            raise LocalTrustBoundaryError(
   104	                f"the resolver returned no archetype for phase {phase} under "
   105	                f"provider 'local' (refusal or coordinator unavailable); "
   106	                f"permitted archetypes: {', '.join(sorted(_LOCAL_TRUSTED_ARCHETYPES))}. "
   107	                "No dispatch attempted."
   108	            )
   109	        if archetype not in _LOCAL_TRUSTED_ARCHETYPES:
   110	            raise LocalTrustBoundaryError(
   111	                f"archetype {archetype!r} (phase {phase}) is outside the 'local' "
   112	                f"provider trust boundary; permitted archetypes: "
   113	                f"{', '.join(sorted(_LOCAL_TRUSTED_ARCHETYPES))}. No dispatch attempted."
   114	            )
   115	
   116	    model = model_override or options.get("model")
   117	    if not model:
   118	        if provider == _LOCAL_PROVIDER and not dry_run:
   119	            # Unreachable in practice (a resolved archetype carries a model), but
   120	            # the invariant is explicit: real local mode never ships a hardcoded
   121	            # model to the endpoint.
   122	            raise LocalTrustBoundaryError(
   123	                f"the resolver returned no model for phase {phase} under provider "
   124	                "'local'. No dispatch attempted."
   125	            )
   126	        model = _FALLBACK_MODELS.get(provider, _DEFAULT_FALLBACK_MODEL)
   127	    if provider != "claude_code" and model in _CLAUDE_ALIASES:
   128	        raise ProviderModelMappingError(provider, model)
   129	
   130	    incoming = PhaseRecord(
   131	        change_id="vendor-neutral-autopilot-smoke",
   132	        phase_name="smoke",
   133	        agent_type="autopilot",
   134	        summary="dry-run provider dispatch smoke",
   135	    )
   136	    prompt = phase_agent._build_prompt(  # noqa: SLF001 - smoke uses canonical helper
   137	        phase,
   138	        {"change_id": "vendor-neutral-autopilot-smoke", "current_phase": phase},
   139	        incoming,
   140	        # Synthetic, to match the synthetic change_id above. `_build_prompt`
   141	        # only renders manifest entries as prompt text and never opens them, so
   142	        # this was a stale label rather than a broken read — but it named a real
   143	        # change (archived 2026-05-16) beside a smoke id that is deliberately
   144	        # fictional, which is the inconsistency the stability guard exists to
   145	        # catch. Fixtures use synthetic ids precisely so they stay
   146	        # distinguishable from paths something actually reads.
   147	        artifacts_manifest=[
   148	            "openspec/changes/vendor-neutral-autopilot-smoke/design.md"
   149	        ],
   150	    )
   151	    system_prompt = options.get("system_prompt")
   152	    if system_prompt:
   153	        prompt = f"{system_prompt}{phase_agent._PROMPT_SEPARATOR}{prompt}"  # noqa: SLF001
   154	
   155	    return PhaseDispatchPayload(
   156	        schema_version=1,
   157	        change_id="vendor-neutral-autopilot-smoke",
   158	        phase=phase,
   159	        provider=provider,
   160	        archetype=archetype,
   161	        model=model,
   162	        prompt=prompt,
   163	        system_prompt=system_prompt,
   164	        isolation=options.get("isolation"),
   165	        expected_outcomes=["complete", "failed"],
   166	    )
   167	
   168	
   169	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   170	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
   171	    parser.add_argument(
   172	        "--provider",
   173	        required=True,
   174	        choices=_SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS,
   175	        help=(
     1	"""Phase sub-agent dispatch with worktree isolation and crash recovery.
     2	
     3	Wraps the harness ``Agent(...)`` invocation behind a dependency-injected
     4	runner so the autopilot driver can call sub-agents for IMPLEMENT,
     5	IMPL_REVIEW, and VALIDATE phases with bounded driver-side state delta.
     6	
     7	Per design D6:
     8	  - run_phase_subagent returns ONLY ``(outcome, handoff_id)`` to the driver.
     9	  - The sub-agent transcript is consumed and discarded inside this module.
    10	  - The next phase reads the structured PhaseRecord via ``read_handoff()``
    11	    or the local fallback file.
    12	
    13	Per local CLI mutation-boundary policy:
    14	  - ``isolation="worktree"`` is set for every write-capable phase.
    15	  - INIT and SUBMIT_PR remain state-only and do not dispatch sub-agents.
    16	
    17	Per design D8:
    18	  - On runner failure or malformed output, retry up to 3 times with the
    19	    SAME incoming PhaseRecord (sub-agent reads partial state from disk).
    20	  - After the third failure, write a phase-failed PhaseRecord to the
    21	    coordinator and raise ``PhaseEscalationError``.
    22	"""

   154	class PhaseEscalationError(Exception):
   155	    """Raised after the sub-agent fails the configured retry budget."""
   156	
   157	    def __init__(
   158	        self,
   159	        phase: str,
   160	        attempts: int,
   161	        last_error: str,
   162	    ) -> None:
   163	        super().__init__(
   164	            f"Phase {phase!r} failed {attempts} attempts; last error: {last_error}"
   165	        )
   166	        self.phase = phase
   167	        self.attempts = attempts
   168	        self.last_error = last_error

   171	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   172	# Public dispatch
   173	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   174	
   175	SubagentRunner = Callable[..., tuple[str, str]]
   176	
   177	
   178	def run_phase_subagent(
   179	    *,
   180	    phase: str,
   181	    state_dict: dict[str, Any],
   182	    incoming_handoff: PhaseRecord,
   183	    subagent_runner: SubagentRunner,
   184	    artifacts_manifest: list[str] | None = None,
   185	    coordinator_writer: Any = None,
   186	    max_attempts: int = _MAX_ATTEMPTS,
   187	) -> tuple[str, str]:
   188	    """Dispatch a phase sub-agent with bounded driver-visible delta.
   189	
   190	    Args:
   191	        phase: Phase id ("IMPLEMENT", "IMPL_REVIEW", "VALIDATE", ...).
   192	        state_dict: Snapshot of LoopState fields the sub-agent prompt may
   193	            reference (change_id, iteration, etc.). Passed by-value to
   194	            keep the driver/sub-agent boundary explicit.
   195	        incoming_handoff: PhaseRecord from the previous phase. Serialized
   196	            into the prompt so the sub-agent can hydrate it via
   197	            ``PhaseRecord.from_handoff_payload`` if needed.
   198	        subagent_runner: Injected callable that actually invokes the
   199	            harness Agent tool. Signature: ``(prompt, options) -> (outcome, handoff_id)``.
   200	            In production the SKILL.md prompt layer provides a runner that
   201	            calls Claude Code's ``Agent(...)`` and parses the result.
   202	        artifacts_manifest: Optional list of repo-relative paths the
   203	            sub-agent should read for context (proposal.md, design.md,
   204	            tasks.md, etc.).
   205	        coordinator_writer: Optional ``try_handoff_write``-shaped callable
   206	            used by the failure path (D8) to record a phase-failed record
   207	            before raising. Defaults to lazy-import via PhaseRecord.
   208	        max_attempts: Override the retry budget. Default 3 per D8.
   209	
   210	    Returns:
   211	        ``(outcome, handoff_id)`` — the only two pieces of information
   212	        propagated back to the driver. Transcript is consumed inside this
   213	        function and never escapes.
   214	
   215	    Raises:
   216	        PhaseEscalationError: After ``max_attempts`` consecutive failures.
   217	    """
   218	    options = _build_options(phase, state_dict)
   219	    prompt = _build_prompt(phase, state_dict, incoming_handoff, artifacts_manifest)

    59	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION is_domain_allowed(
    60	    p_agent_id TEXT,
    61	    p_domain TEXT
    62	)
    63	RETURNS JSONB
    64	LANGUAGE plpgsql
    65	AS $$
    66	DECLARE
    67	    v_profile_id UUID;
    68	    v_policy RECORD;
    69	    v_allowed BOOLEAN := false;
    70	    v_reason TEXT := 'no_matching_policy';
    71	    v_policy_id UUID;
    72	BEGIN
    73	    -- Get agent's profile ID
    74	    SELECT pa.profile_id INTO v_profile_id
    75	    FROM agent_profile_assignments pa
    76	    WHERE pa.agent_id = p_agent_id;
    77	
    78	    -- Check policies: profile-specific first, then global (NULL profile_id)
    79	    -- Higher priority (lower number) wins
    80	    FOR v_policy IN
    81	        SELECT np.*
    82	        FROM network_policies np
    83	        WHERE np.enabled = true
    84	          AND (np.profile_id = v_profile_id OR np.profile_id IS NULL)
    85	          AND (
    86	              p_domain = np.domain_pattern
    87	              OR p_domain LIKE REPLACE(np.domain_pattern, '*', '%')
    88	          )
    89	        ORDER BY
    90	            CASE WHEN np.profile_id IS NOT NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,  -- profile-specific first
    91	            np.priority ASC
    92	        LIMIT 1
    93	    LOOP
    94	        v_allowed := (v_policy.action = 'allow');
    95	        v_reason := v_policy.action;
    96	        v_policy_id := v_policy.id;
    97	    END LOOP;
    98	
    99	    -- Log the access attempt
   100	    INSERT INTO network_access_log (agent_id, domain, allowed, policy_id, reason)
   101	    VALUES (p_agent_id, p_domain, v_allowed, v_policy_id, v_reason);
   102	
   103	    RETURN jsonb_build_object(
   104	        'allowed', v_allowed,
   105	        'domain', p_domain,
   106	        'reason', v_reason,
   107	        'policy_id', v_policy_id
   108	    );
   109	END;
   110	$$;

     1	"""Network access policy service for Agent Coordinator.
     2	
     3	Provides domain-level access control for agent network requests.
     4	Policies are per-profile with global fallbacks.
     5	"""
     6	
     7	from dataclasses import dataclass
     8	from typing import Any
     9	
    10	from .config import get_config
    11	from .db import DatabaseClient, get_db
    12	
    13	
    14	@dataclass
    15	class AccessDecision:
    16	    """Result of a domain access check."""
    17	
    18	    allowed: bool
    19	    domain: str
    20	    reason: str | None = None
    21	    policy_id: str | None = None
    22	
    23	    @classmethod
    24	    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "AccessDecision":
    25	        return cls(
    26	            allowed=data.get("allowed", False),
    27	            domain=data.get("domain", ""),
    28	            reason=data.get("reason"),
    29	            policy_id=str(data["policy_id"]) if data.get("policy_id") else None,
    30	        )
    31	
    32	
    33	class NetworkPolicyService:
    34	    """Service for network access policy enforcement."""
    35	
    36	    def __init__(self, db: DatabaseClient | None = None):
    37	        self._db = db
    38	
    39	    @property
    40	    def db(self) -> DatabaseClient:
    41	        if self._db is None:
    42	            self._db = get_db()
    43	        return self._db
    44	
    45	    async def check_domain(
    46	        self,
    47	        domain: str,
    48	        agent_id: str | None = None,
    49	    ) -> AccessDecision:
    50	        """Check if an agent is allowed to access a domain.
    51	
    52	        Args:
    53	            domain: The domain to check (e.g., 'github.com')
    54	            agent_id: Agent making the request (default: from config)
    55	
    56	        Returns:
    57	            AccessDecision with allowed status and reason
    58	        """
    59	        config = get_config()
    60	        agent_id = agent_id or config.agent.agent_id
    61	
    62	        try:
    63	            result = await self.db.rpc(
    64	                "is_domain_allowed",
    65	                {
    66	                    "p_agent_id": agent_id,
    67	                    "p_domain": domain,
    68	                },
    69	            )
    70	            return AccessDecision.from_dict(result)
    71	        except Exception:
    72	            # On error, apply default policy
    73	            default_allowed = config.network_policy.default_policy == "allow"
    74	            return AccessDecision(
    75	                allowed=default_allowed,
    76	                domain=domain,
    77	                reason=f"default_policy:{config.network_policy.default_policy}",
    78	            )
    79	
    80	
    81	# Global service instance
    82	_network_policy_service: NetworkPolicyService | None = None
    83	
    84	
    85	def get_network_policy_service() -> NetworkPolicyService:
    86	    """Get the global network policy service instance."""
    87	    global _network_policy_service
    88	    if _network_policy_service is None:
    89	        _network_policy_service = NetworkPolicyService()
    90	    return _network_policy_service
